title: الأَسْمَاءُ الْمَوْصُولَةُ
blocks: Relative pronouns prevent repetition and allow Arabic sentences to carry more precise information.
[callout] Join the ideas: أَعْرِفُ الْوَلَدَ الَّذِي يَسْكُنُ هُنَا. I know the boy who lives here.
## Use the chapter at the depth you need

TABLE: Meaning | Form | Used with | Example // who / which / that | الَّذِي | masculine singular | الطَّالِبُ الَّذِي فَازَ // who / which / that | الَّتِي | feminine singular | الطَّالِبَةُ الَّتِي فَازَتْ // the two who | اللَّذَانِ | masculine dual — nominative | الطَّالِبَانِ اللَّذَانِ نَجَحَا // the two who | اللَّتَانِ | feminine dual — nominative | الطَّالِبَتَانِ اللَّتَانِ نَجَحَتَا // who | الَّذِينَ | masculine or mixed human plural | الطُّلَّابُ الَّذِينَ حَضَرُوا // who | اللَّاتِي / اللَّائِي | feminine human plural | الطَّالِبَاتُ اللَّاتِي حَضَرْنَ
[callout] House form: this lesson uses اللَّاتِي as the main feminine plural form. اللَّائِي is also correct and may appear in authentic texts.
[example] الطَّالِبُ الَّذِي يَدْرُسُ كَثِيرًا مُجْتَهِدٌ. The student who studies a lot is hardworking.
[callout] Terminology: the noun being described is the antecedent . The words after the relative pronoun form the relative clause .
## The relative pronoun agrees with the noun
[callout] Agreement is cumulative: check the antecedent, choose the correct relative pronoun, then make the verb agree with the person or group inside the relative clause.
## Definite nouns normally take a relative pronoun
[example] جَاءَ الطَّالِبُ الَّذِي فَازَ. The student who won came.
[example] جَاءَ طَالِبٌ فَازَ فِي الْمُسَابَقَةِ. A student who won the competition came.
Arabic often links the clause directly without an explicit relative pronoun after an indefinite noun.
[callout] Do not overgeneralise: English frequently uses “who/which/that” after both definite and indefinite nouns. Arabic treats these structures differently.
Subject pronouns help identify who performs the action inside the relative clause.
Possessive endings can appear inside a relative clause.
Object pronouns can refer back to the antecedent.
Demonstratives can introduce a noun followed by a relative clause.
Arabic often uses a pronoun inside the relative clause that refers back to the antecedent, especially when the antecedent is the object or appears after a preposition.
[example] هٰذَا هُوَ الْكِتَابُ الَّذِي قَرَأْتُهُ. This is the book that I read.
[example] هٰذِهِ هِيَ الْمَدْرَسَةُ الَّتِي أَدْرُسُ فِيهَا. This is the school in which I study.
[ar] هٰذِهِ هِيَ الْمَدْرَسَةُ الَّتِي أَدْرُسُ فِيهَا.
[callout] What refers back? In قَرَأْتُهُ , the object ending ـهُ refers back to الْكِتَابُ . In فِيهَا , ـهَا refers back to الْمَدْرَسَةُ .
### Choose the antecedent, relative pronoun and clause
## Find the antecedent and the extra information

[ar] فِي مَدْرَسَتِنَا طُلَّابٌ كَثِيرُونَ. الطَّالِبُ الَّذِي فَازَ فِي الْمُسَابَقَةِ اسْمُهُ سَامِرٌ. وَالطَّالِبَةُ الَّتِي كَتَبَتِ الْقِصَّةَ اسْمُهَا لَيْلَى. هٰؤُلَاءِ هُمُ الطُّلَّابُ الَّذِينَ يُسَاعِدُونَ زُمَلَاءَهُمْ، وَتِلْكَ هِيَ الْمُعَلِّمَةُ الَّتِي تُشَجِّعُهُمْ دَائِمًا. أُحِبُّ الْمَكْتَبَةَ الَّتِي أَقْرَأُ فِيهَا، وَهٰذَا هُوَ الْكِتَابُ الَّذِي قَرَأْتُهُ فِي الْأُسْبُوعِ الْمَاضِي.

There are many students in our school. The student who won the competition is called Samer. The female student who wrote the story is called Layla. These are the students who help their classmates, and that is the teacher who always encourages them. I like the library in which I read, and this is the book that I read last week.
Describe a person, place, book or school experience using at least:
- one connection to a demonstrative or possessive structure
Write 8–10 Arabic sentences about your school, family, a person you admire or a book you enjoyed. Use at least six relative pronouns.

[callout] Self-edit checklist: Does the relative pronoun agree with the antecedent? Is the verb agreement correct? Is a resumptive pronoun needed? Have you avoided repeating the same short sentence pattern?
[callout] Context rule: authentic examples should clarify the grammar, not become long texts that delay the teaching point.
## Why this grammar matters for confident Arabic communication
Relative clauses help identify which person, object or place a speaker means.
Students must follow long noun phrases and reference chains.
Relative clauses extend answers and reduce repetitive short sentences.
They improve cohesion, precision and sentence variety.

## Common mistakes and how to repair them
Human masculine or mixed plural uses الَّذِينَ .
The object pronoun refers back to the book.
Indefinite antecedents often take a directly linked clause.
